newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: J.P. Morgan tips Moody's upgrade for Philippines.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan tips Moody's upgrade for Philippines.

text.p: International brokerage firm J.P. Morgan Securities Inc is expecting Moody's Investors Service to upgrade its rating on the Philippines this year, a J.P. Morgan outlook paper released on Sunday said.

The ratings change would follow an upgrade made by Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) last month. S&P raised its Philippine debt paper rating on February 21 to BB plus, or one notch below investment grade, from the previous level of BB.
"The (S&P) rating will set the stage for a similar upgrade by Moody's from Ba2 to Ba1, expected this year," JP Morgan analyst Karim Adbel Motaal said.
He said constraints highlighted by S&P including a low tax yield should be addressed by the tax reform bill, which is likely to be passed by May this year.
The bill seeks to improve the personal and corporate tax collection by expanding the taxpayers' base.
In a separate research paper, Bankers Trust Research analyst Cristina Infante said the recent S&P upgrade should encourage the issuance of more infrastructure-related bonds.
She said dollar-denominated bonds would be the most favoured instruments in financing the privatisation programme of the government.
Infante further recommended a buy on long-dated power-related issues including those floated by the state-owned National Power Corp before the upgrade.
"We expect these issues to continue to benefit as the perception of the Philippines' sovereign credit improves over time," she said.
